Bank of America (NYSE:BAC), the second-largest bank in the U.S. by assets, will report its third-quarter earnings results on Wednesday, Oct. 14, before the market opens. Management, led by CEO Brian Moynihan, will then host a live conference call with Wall Street analysts.

Banks had been benefiting from market rotation earlier this year, but have come under pressure more recently due to soaring bond yields, which increase funding costs and can weigh on loan growth and credit quality.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Banks, including Bank of America, are now widely underperforming the broader market this year. Is Bank of America stock a buy ahead of its third-quarter earnings report?

Image source: The Motley Fool.

Likely will come down to Net Interest Income

Heading into third-quarter results, Bank of America has lowered expectations for some of its businesses, including investment banking and trading.

At a conference in mid-September, Moynihan told analysts that investment banking fees could be down 10% year over year, while trading revenue may come in flat.

"What we're seeing is the market generally in investment banking is down 10%," said Moynihan, referencing data from Dealogic, according to CNBC. "We're not as well positioned in some of the businesses that have more activity, so we'll be down probably a bit more than that."

So this will likely put net interest income (NII) into focus. NII is the spread revenue that banks earn between what they pay on interest-bearing liabilities, such as deposits, and what they accrue on interest-earning assets, such as loans. It's a key revenue driver for most banks.

On the second-quarter earnings call, Bank of America's CFO Alastair Borthwick told analysts to expect full-year NII to be toward the upper end of its previous guidance of 6% to 8% annual growth.

Borthwick said that's based on modest loan and deposit growth and one rate hike in 2026. However, there's already been one rate hike, and there still could be another.

Bank of America is asset-sensitive, meaning NII should benefit in a rising-rate environment because assets will reprice faster than liabilities, especially its large, low-cost deposit base, which should see a more modest increase in deposit pricing.

Bank of America is known for having one of the strongest, if not the strongest, deposit bases from a funding perspective, meaning it tends to have a more stable, lower-cost deposit base than its peers.

Analysts Raise Targets on Securitize, Coinbase, Robinhood; BofA Cuts eToro

StoneX raised its price target on Securitize (NYSE: $SECZ) by 50% on Monday, adding to a run of target changes on crypto-linked stocks this month ahead of third-quarter earnings.

StoneX analyst Mark Palmer lifted his target to $18 from $12 and kept a Buy rating. He argued that Securitize's new tokenized stock trading platform, launched last Thursday, will open a major new revenue stream. Shares fell about 10% Monday morning, leaving the new target roughly 45% above current prices. Palmer said the market still values Securitize like a tokenization vendor, even though it now operates as a market.

Management said on its August earnings call that most tokenization revenue came from integration fees, meaning little of the $5.3 billion in second-quarter transaction volume was monetized, according to StoneX. The new platform lets the company earn fees on transactions and servicing, with possible collateral revenue later. Last week's launch put stocks including Apple (NASDAQ: $AAPL), Nvidia (NASDAQ: $NVDA) and Tesla (NASDAQ: $TSLA) on Solana, backed one-for-one by underlying shares and settling in USDC (CRYPTO: $USDC).

More From Cryptoprowl:

Cardano Founder Hoskinson Says Midnight Will Surpass Zcash, Urges Gemini to List ADA

Stacks Founder Warns Bitcoin Security Breach Could Hit Entire Crypto Market

Coinbase Targets Banks As Institutional Crypto Adoption Grows

Crypto Heavyweights Back OKX at $25B Valuation

StoneX projects revenue of nearly $120 million in 2027 and almost $200 million in 2028, about 65% annual growth. Its $18 target implies a 14.5-times enterprise-value-to-revenue multiple on the 2028 forecast.

Bank of America (NYSE: $BAC) analyst Craig Siegenthaler made his own moves on Oct. 5. He raised Robinhood (NASDAQ: $HOOD) to $156 from $140 and Coinbase (NASDAQ: $COIN) to $203 from $174, keeping Buy ratings on both. He cut eToro (NASDAQ: $ETOR) to $39 from $46 with a Neutral rating.

Expectations differ by company. Robinhood is expected to report third-quarter earnings of $0.64 per share on revenue near $1.4 billion, and has beaten EPS estimates in each of its last 11 quarters. Coinbase is projected to post a $0.20 per-share loss on about $1.77 billion in revenue, after missing estimates in each of the last three quarters. eToro is forecast at $0.40 per share on roughly $203 million.

Commentary tied the Coinbase increase partly to expected stablecoin revenue after the Federal Reserve's September rate increase, even as near-term trading volume forecasts were trimmed.

Key Stats for Salesforce Stock

Price change for Salesforce stock in the last 6 months: 33%

$CRM Stock Price as of Oct. 9: $229

52-Week High: $269

$CRM Stock Price Target: $283

What Happened?

BofA Securities upgraded Salesforce (CRM:NYSE) to Buy from Underperform on Monday and raised its price target to $285 from $160.

The firm dropped its earlier worry that AI would push Salesforce aside. After talking with chief information officers, BofA said large companies are unlikely to replace platforms that hold their business logic, data, workflows, and compliance rules.

In its view, AI should make companies lean more on these platforms.

BofA asked two questions. Does Salesforce have a credible AI strategy? And can AI grow customer spending on the platform? It answered yes to both.

Cash flow also played a part, given Salesforce generated over $15 billion in levered free cash flow over the last twelve months.

That works out to an 8% free cash flow yield. BofA said this supports a slight valuation premium.

CRM Stock Revenue, EBIT and Free Cash Flow Estimates in Billion USD (TIKR)

The new target uses 16 times calendar 2027 enterprise value to free cash flow. The old target used 9 times, while the peer average is higher at 15 times.

Other analysts are also positive.

Yorkville Ives started coverage at Outperform with a $290 target.

Oppenheimer kept Outperform with a $275 target.

UBS raised its target to $260 but kept its rating Neutral.

Citizens kept Market Outperform with a $315 target.

What the Market Is Telling Us About Salesforce Stock

Salesforce stock has been under pressure as fears that AI would hurt software companies have grown. This upgrade takes the opposite view, and CRM stock now has a bull case built on trust and data, in addition to growth.

The latest results back that up.

Q2 revenue was $11.35 billion, up 11%.

Agentforce ARR hit $1.5 billion.

Free cash flow was $1.1 billion, up 81%.

The company raised its full-year revenue guidance by about $300 million.

Management also said net new AOV growth was the strongest in four years and attrition was near its lowest level ever.

Certain risks remain, as license revenue is still volatile. Management called a marketing recovery too early to call a trend. Analysts also disagree on how much upside is left.

For now, a shift in how Wall Street sees AI is driving Salesforce stock.

What happens across this Global Week Ahead?

A backdrop of high energy costs and rising central bank rates, while

The latest U.S. and China macro data

Wall Street Q3 earnings, and

Turbulent bond markets point to a packed week ahead

Next are Reuters' five world market themes, re-ordered for equity traders—

(1) U.S. Q3 Earnings Season Kicks Off — with the Major Banks, of Course

It's the start of Q3 U.S. earnings season, and who better to kick things off than the banks?

Four of the six largest U.S. lenders, JPMorgan Chase JPM, Goldman Sachs GS, Citigroup C and Wells Fargo WFC, report on Tuesday, followed a day after by Morgan Stanley MS and Bank of America BAC.

Earnings are ‌expected to rise up to +20% relative to last year.

Still, the surge in Treasury yields to multi-decade highs has hurt shares — the KBW Bank Index is down around -13% from its peak in August.

Investors will be looking for signs that the recent spike in government borrowing costs may curb dealmaking and lending growth, as well as pressure funding costs across the industry.

(2) U.S. and French Government Bond Yields Keep Surging

Surging government borrowing costs are clearly luring some investors back to bonds as evidenced by the strong demand at the latest U.S. and Japanese auctions.

But do you really want to catch a falling knife?

That's the question for traders in the coming week as the bond selloff shows few signs of abating.

U.S. and French bond yields have hit fresh 24-year highs and market volatility is high.

The French-German 10-year bond yield spread, at around 136 basis points, was below 100 bps a month ago.

The speed and scale of the rise in the French risk premium is hurting Italian peers, the euro and European shares.

It's also led to some finger-pointing at the role of hedge funds — that fast-money group that has stepped up its presence in systemically important bond markets of late.

(3) On Wednesday, U.S. Consumer Price Inflation (CPI) Data for September Lands

A fresh look at U.S. inflation on Wednesday will be among the last key data released before the Federal Reserve decides whether to hike interest rates again to contain high prices.

The September CPI is set to show a 0.6% rise on a monthly basis. The core measure, excluding volatile energy and food components, is estimated to increase just 0.2%, according to a Reuters poll.

Thursday's Producer Price Index (PPI) numbers will further flesh out the inflation picture. Retail sales data is also out that day.

Core CPI for August rose at its fastest pace in four months, helping cement the Fed's first rate hike since 2023.

Bets on another hike when the Fed meets in late October have fallen back. A hot CPI report could change that.

Warren Buffett earned the nickname the Oracle of Omaha, with the 6,099,294% gain of Berkshire Hathaway (NYSE: BRKA)(NYSE: BRKB) under his leadership showing why. The S&P 500 index (SNPINDEX: ^GSPC) rose 46,061% over the same period. Looking at Buffett's approach can provide a good foundation for your own investment approach.

Simply put, Buffett liked to buy well-run businesses while they were attractively priced. But the real secret sauce is that he held for the long term, which allowed him to benefit from a business's growth over time. American Express (NYSE: AXP) and Coca-Cola (NYSE: KO) highlight why you don't want to overlook this step, even if it means holding through bear markets. Chevron (NYSE: CVX) and Bank of America (NYSE: BAC), two relatively new purchases, are building their track records.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.
A quick look at four long-term Buffett holdings

Before looking at the gains Buffett achieved with Chevron, Bank of America, American Express, and Coca-Cola, there are a few ground rules to keep in mind for each example. You wouldn't be able to buy exactly when Buffett did because regulatory filings are delayed. To keep things simple, the start of the year following the first purchase will be used. The most recent investment period is going to be used, noting that he invested in American Express two times. And only stock purchases will be featured, since you couldn't buy the preferred investments he's made, including the one in Bank of America. With that said, here are the impressive returns some of these dividend stocks have provided to Buffett.

Coca-Cola: 1989

Buffett began buying Coca-Cola in 1988 and continued his original purchases into 1989. We'll use 1989 as the starting date. Today, Coca-Cola is one of the world's largest consumer staples companies, selling soda and other beverages. It has industry-leading brands, marketing, product development, and distribution. A $1,000 investment made at the start of 1989 would be worth roughly $18,000 as of this writing. That's a 1,700% return and doesn't include dividend reinvestment. That lags just behind the S&P 500. Add in dividend reinvestment, however, and that $1k would be worth an even more impressive $43,000, which is a shockingly large return of 4,200%.

In July, Bank of America (NYSE: BAC) raised its quarterly dividend by 14%, to $0.32 per share, or $1.28 annually. That gives it a decent yield of about 2.4%.

So, how many shares of the bank stock would you need to own to collect $1,000 a year in dividend income?

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.

It's a straightforward calculation. $1,000 divided by $1.28 is 781.25. So that's the number of shares needed to generate that annual income amount. At the current price of $52.75 per share, acquiring that many shares would cost about $41,211. That's a lot of money to invest just for $1,000 a year in passive income.

Are there any other reasons it might be worth it to make this investment? Well, the stock is trading about 17.5% below its 52-week high. Given the company's history of growth, is this a good time to start building such a position in Bank of America stock?

Bank of America was hit this year by softer Wall Street revenue guidance, regulatory pressures, and macroeconomic concerns related to rising yields and interest rates. Like BofA, many bank stocks are down this year.

But Bank of America remains one of the world's largest financial companies, and offers investment banking and investment management along with its retail banking operations. It has a reputation for being one of the best-run banks in the world.

Keep in mind, too, that Bank of America has built a strong track record of annual dividend increases, now spanning about 13 years, so those dividends are likely -- though not guaranteed -- to continue increasing.

So, if you're looking for a solid dividend payer in the financial services sector with a lot of upside potential, this may be a good stock to own.
